subarea.label: Ownership, Possession and Occupancy
subarea.description: Legal and factual relationships between parties and the property.

buyer.definition: A sub property of participant. The participant/person/organization that bought the object.

customer.definition: Party placing the order or paying the invoice.

occupancy.definition:
The allowed total occupancy for the accommodation in persons (including infants etc). For individual accommodations, this is not necessarily the legal maximum but defines the permitted usage as per the contractual agreement (e.g. a double room used by a single person).
Typical unit code(s): C62 for person.

owner.definition: A person or organization who owns this Thing.

ownership_funding_info.definition: For an [[Organization]] (often but not necessarily a [[NewsMediaOrganization]]), a description of organizational ownership structure; funding and grants. In a news/media setting, this is with particular reference to editorial independence.   Note that the [[funder]] is also available and can be used to make basic funder information machine-readable.

owns.definition: Things owned by the organization or person.

provider.definition: The service provider, service operator, or service performer; the goods producer. Another party (a seller) may offer those services or goods on behalf of the provider. A provider may also serve as the seller.

seller.definition: An entity which offers (sells / leases / lends / loans) the services / goods.  A seller may also be a provider.

candidate_concepts.source_definition: The name of the owner of the property being sold.
A list of expenses for the property paid for by the owner as opposed to the tenant (e.g., Water, Trash, Electric).
A text description of the manner in which title to a property is held (e.g., Trust, Corporation, Joint Tenant, Individual).

A list of services or items that the tenant is responsible to pay.
A pick list describing the current status of tenants or lack of tenants at the property.

Text remarks that may be displayed to the public. In an MLS, it is the field where information is entered for the public. This information is intended to be visible online. This is typically information that describes the selling points of the building and/or land for sale. Local conditions and rules will determine what such content can contain. Generally, any information pertaining to entry to the property, the seller and/or tenant, or listing member contact information is excluded. In other systems, these remarks will be determined by local business rules.
Describes a variety of rent-like cash flows from tenants that are not a part of the traditional base rent.
A fee paid by the homeowner to the homeowner association that is used for upkeep of common areas, the neighborhood or other association-related benefits.
The annual expense that is not paid directly by the tenant and is included in the Operating Expense calculations.

A type of ownership in a property that is composed of an individual lot or unit and a share of the ownership or use of common areas. A Common Interest Development (CID) is usually governed by a recorded set of Covenants, Conditions & Restrictions (CC&Rs).
The type or level of service the listing member will be providing to the selling homeowner (e.g., Full Service, Limited Service, Entry Only). This will typically be a single selection.

The annual expense that is not paid directly by the tenant and is included in the Operating Expense calculations. This is for an individual manager. Use ProfessionalManagementExpense for a management company.
Remarks that may contain security or proprietary information and should be restricted from public view.
A fee paid by the homeowner to the second of two homeowner associations that is used for upkeep of common areas, the neighborhood or other association-related benefits.
The name of the homeowner association.
